clue.text: Worldly sailor's a decent sort

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
worldly things are of the earth rather than of heaven

explanation.surface: A well-travelled seaman turns out to be a thoroughly decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse clue order: the sailor comes first in the answer, and the worldly part follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from the Sermon on the Mount, describes a person who is honest, kind and dependable.

clue.text: A staff raise oft renegotiated in this situation

indicators.note: a renegotiated deal has its terms rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pay rise for employees keeps being reopened for negotiation, which is the current situation at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of affairs is the prevailing set of circumstances, which is what a situation is.

clue.text: Pulses taken in part of hospital where ill wander around

indicators.note: letters that wander have strayed from their places, so they are jumbled
something taken in is held inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the fodder; the answer needs an S beside these letters, as if the clue had said ills
the Ear, Nose and Throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Beans and peas are brought into a hospital ward where sick patients roam about.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT sits inside a jumble of the patients' letters, but the word ill supplies only three of the four letters needed; the setter must have meant ills.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and lentils are a common example.

clue.text: Nicest boy can come out with a dirty word

indicators.note: letters that come out are released from their order and may land in any arrangement

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Even the most well-behaved lad is liable to let slip a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscenity is an offensive expletive, the kind of word called dirty in everyday speech.

clue.text: Tried an unusual part exchange

indicators.note: an unusual version departs from the normal form, so the letters take a different order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempted an odd swap deal when buying something.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as partial payment for a new one, which Britons call part exchange.

clue.text: Gem displays an ephemeral dazzle

indicators.note: what the following words display is a run of letters on show within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A precious stone gives off a brief, fleeting sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, a classic example of a gem.

clue.text: Boxer has two-part defence

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer
the prefix meaning two

explanation.surface: A fighter has a defensive strategy with two phases.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been elsewhere, used by an accused person as a defence.

clue.text: Faint song disappearing here?

blocks.note: a faint sound or line is thin
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A quiet melody fades away to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'vanish into thin air'; the question mark flags that it describes a place only figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that vanish without trace are said to disappear into this, so it is the notional place of disappearance.

clue.text: Call up cases where Superman changes?

blocks.note: to call someone up is to ring them
boxes are containers

explanation.surface: Phone the people who hold the cases where the superhero switches into costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Kent famously ducks into a phone booth to become Superman, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Public phone kiosks are the comic-book spot where Clark Kent swaps clothes to become the superhero.

clue.text: Memory loss means mixing up incidents and appointments initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it
mixing things up puts them out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the heads of the two nouns, skipping the joining word

explanation.surface: Forgetfulness leads a person to confuse events with scheduled meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a verb linking definition and wordplay, but it is fodder for the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total loss of memory.

clue.text: East Germany provided international church building

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation
D for Deutschland, the international vehicle code
provided that means if
I is a standard abbreviation for international
the Church of England

explanation.surface: East Germany supplied a building for a worldwide church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Germany' reads as the old country but splits into two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, so it is a grand word for a building.

clue.text: Banish former lover to pointless little island

indicators.note: pointless means without a point, so a compass point letter is dropped

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
an isle is a small island

explanation.surface: Send an old flame away to a tiny, worthless island.
explanation.walkthrough: The point removed is S, south, from the island word.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to expel them from their country, which is to banish them.

clue.text: Time to order heartless wipe out

indicators.note: something heartless has lost its heart, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
to dictate is to give orders

explanation.surface: It is time for someone cruel to be told to destroy something.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the seven-letter order word is its middle T, which drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, which is the sense of wipe out.

clue.text: Designed by Vogue editor

blocks.note: a vogue is a fashion
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Something was created by the editor of Vogue magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital V makes it look like the magazine, but here it is just the common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or make it, so fashioned means designed.

clue.text: Dress up husband for fun!

indicators.note: up suggests turning a word on its head, so it reads backwards here

blocks.note: to trim is to decorate or dress
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Dress up one's husband in costume for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' looks like a single phrase, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay as the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is amusement and laughter, which is what fun brings.

clue.text: Mister Brown takes cover in part of New York

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a mister is a man
a hat covers the head
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A man called Mr Brown shelters somewhere in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Brown' reads as a name, but the two words give separate pieces with the cover placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is one of the five boroughs that make up New York City.

clue.text: Stale and oddly stuffy without feminine input

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken out
doing something oddly means doing it in a strange way, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for feminine; the input is the letter it contributes

explanation.surface: A room is musty and strangely airless when no woman has had a hand in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but it signals a jumble once one F is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusty describes something smelling stale and musty from age or lack of air.

clue.text: Drives, breaking US limit

indicators.note: something breaking falls apart, and its letters are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist drives over the American speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drives' looks like a verb about cars but is a plural noun meaning motivations.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur action, much as drives or urges push someone on.

clue.text: Kind of accident that happens in rounders?

definitions.text: Kind of accident that happens in rounders?

blocks.note: surface: a type of road crash where the driver leaves the scene
setter's reading: in rounders, a batting game, the batter strikes the ball and then races off

explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British children's bat-and-ball game similar to baseball; the phrase describes both a motoring offence and what every batter does.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a collision where the driver flees, and literally the two actions of a batter in rounders.

clue.text: Goin' on about one for fixing locks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: harping on means going on about something; the apostrophe shows the dropped G, as in the clue
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clipped bit of speech complaining about a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a pin used to hold hair, or locks, in place.

clue.text: No coming back in drunk this evening!

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read in the other direction
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vow not to return home drunk tonight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the present or coming evening, so it means this evening.

clue.text: Religious Education student has to make money to study again

blocks.note: RE is the British school subject abbreviation
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: A religious studies pupil must take a job before going back to their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn is to learn something a second time, which is to study it again.

clue.text: Musical girl is allowed to avoid broadcast activity

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard over the air, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: Annie is the orphan girl of the stage musical
one may do what is allowed
to shun is to avoid

explanation.surface: A girl in a show gets permission to dodge being on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the three pieces run together into the answer; the spelling of each is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness, a state of being active and spirited.

clue.text: Check car is on time

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Check whether the car is running to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, so it is a check.

clue.text: Unprepared lad troubled by International Baccalaureate

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
IB is the standard abbreviation for the school qualification

explanation.surface: A boy who has not done his revision is worried by his IB exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-lib describes something improvised on the spot, without preparation.

clue.text: Assemble a whole number?

blocks.note: first meaning: gather people or animals together
second meaning: raise a fraction to the next integer

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a verb phrase in disguise: you do this to a decimal to get a whole number, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to gather together, and also to raise a figure to the next integer.

clue.text: Access to the French cakes

blocks.note: a gate is a way in
aux is French for to the, before a plural

explanation.surface: Way in to the French pastry shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateaux are rich cream cakes, the French plural of gâteau.

clue.text: Isn't it awfully good to find a number of workers that can't be evicted?

definitions.note: describes the people rather than naming them; the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are put into a poor, jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
G is the abbreviation for good
ten is a number
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about how marvellous it is to employ staff who can never be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully good' reads as a phrase meaning very good, but 'good' is a single letter added to the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Under British law a sitting tenant is one already in occupation with protected rights, so hard to remove.
